What advanced composition and visual hierarchy means here: Visual hierarchy is the order in which a composition invites attention. How the relationship changes the result: A focal area becomes strong through a noticeable relationship with nearby areas; quiet space and repeated directions can lead attention to later stops. Choice and tradeoff: A steep hierarchy reads quickly but can silence later areas. A shallow hierarchy can feel open but may make a precise route harder to read. ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g9-arts-and-music-u01-l02

Lesson focus: advanced composition and visual hierarchy

Title: Three Stops — an annotated visual-hierarchy model

Creator: Manuel Academy curriculum team

Role: technique model, worked artistic example, partial exemplar, and one possible finished exemplar

The delivered SVG shows a flat start, an intermediate state using placement, value, scale, and isolation, a finished three-stop visual path, and a triangle-first variation. The variation proves that the model’s exact arrangement is not the answer.

Technique sequence: state a focal point; arrange large masses; create the strongest useful difference at the focal point; repeat or direct a feature to build a path; step back or blur-and-glance; revise one variable at a time. Common trouble spot: increasing every contrast equally can make all parts compete.

Access parallel: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For a tactile route, use three raised or cut-paper shapes. Make one shape noticeably rougher, taller, or more isolated, connect the shapes with string, and trace the intended order by touch.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party work is included.
critique_criteria: All required evidence is present; one note may be brief, but the guided pair, original study, two variables, intermediate state, path check, revision decision, reflection, and critique can each be located.
At least two named variables create observable emphasis related to the intended focal point, and the learner cites where the eye or hand moves next using evidence from the work.
The learner states the intended order and connects specific value, scale, placement, isolation, repetition, edge, or direction evidence to that intention.
The record shows an intermediate state, one criteria-based check, and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the work.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a labelled visual, tactile, constructed, or accessible digital work to preserve the making target; prose alone does not claim visual or material technique evidence. You may describe the work in writing and have one trusted adult verify a physical artifact without photographing you or your home. No microphone, camera, or recording is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres a visual element (advanced composition and visual hierarchy). Provide tactile, raised-line, or high-relief equivalents, enlarged and high-contrast print, and a verbal description route. Never make colour discrimination alone carry a criterion — pair any colour judgement with value, label, or texture.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.fallback: Use the supplied full verbal description and the tactile three-shape-and-string route. The reference is a committed Academy asset, not a teacher-supplied or outside-search requirement.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce the work to a three-value map. Label each major area light, middle, or dark; circle every large jump. Keep one large jump and lower the others in a fresh thumbnail. Use three forms and only pencil pressure. Create one dark-light jump at the intended first stop; keep the other forms middle or pale. Check yourself: Squint or use the tactile value labels: can you locate one strongest difference? New attempt: Make a new thumbnail with different placements and run a new three-second check. Route 2: Cover the work except for the intended focal point and one competing area. Compare only those two; choose whether value, scale, isolation, edge, or direction should separate them. On scrap paper, redraw the two areas and change exactly one chosen variable. Check yourself: Name the changed variable before deciding which area arrives first. New attempt: Return all areas in a fresh thumbnail and test the intended path without the model in view.
extension: Apply advanced composition and visual hierarchy under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on advanced composition and visual hierarchy rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_registry.meaning: The arrangement and relationship of parts within the edges of a work.
The order in which a composition invites attention.
The area an artist intends as the strongest or first stop.
The open area around and between forms, used here to create isolation.
A bounded visual or tactile area used as a compositional element.

technique_registry.meaning: Create emphasis by controlling the size and location of light-dark differences.
Create emphasis by controlling relative size without assuming largest must lead.
Create emphasis through location, spacing, clustering, and isolation.
Use a brief first-impression check to record the observed order of attention before judging it.
Make a small, quick composition study to test relationships without aiming for polish.

age_policy.privacy: Private work and self-critique carry full credit; no public display, identifiable media, account, or recording is required.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: A focal area becomes strong through a noticeable relationship with nearby areas; quiet space and repeated directions can lead attention to later stops.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: A steep hierarchy reads quickly but can silence later areas. A shallow hierarchy can feel open but may make a precise route harder to read. Worked example: A small dark isolated form can lead a large pale form because the local value jump and open space are stronger than size alone. Non-example: Making every edge, colour, and value equally strong creates competition rather than a controllable path.

reference_registry.title: Three Stops — verbal and tactile description
reference_registry.creator: Manuel Academy curriculum team

model_registry.notice: Similar visual weight leaves the first stop unsettled.
model_registry.creator_choice: Use similar mid-values and even spacing as a deliberate non-example.

model_registry.notice: Isolation and the largest value jump make the small circle arrive first.
model_registry.creator_choice: Keep the large triangle pale so size does not automatically win.

model_registry.notice: A curved directional line and repeated stripe angle carry attention through three stops.
model_registry.creator_choice: The circle-first route is one solution; the alternate panel makes a triangle-first route with different choices.

technique_sequence.action: State the intended effect or question before making or judging.
technique_sequence.notice: The statement creates a criterion that can be checked.
technique_sequence.why: Arts evidence is interpreted in relation to purpose, not personal taste.

technique_sequence.action: Identify or set up the relevant placement, scale, value, edge, isolation, repetition, and direction.
technique_sequence.notice: Locate the first relationship that can be observed in advanced composition and visual hierarchy.
technique_sequence.why: A focal area becomes strong through a noticeable relationship with nearby areas; quiet space and repeated directions can lead attention to later stops.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Transfer the idea to a fresh work, excerpt, source detail, or project decision.
technique_sequence.notice: Close the model or cue before the independent decision.

technique_sequence.action: Check against criteria and choose a revision or a reasoned decision to keep the result.
technique_sequence.notice: Cite a location, moment, event, or process fact before judging.
technique_sequence.why: Evidence protects creative variation and learner authority.

work_blocks.title: Guided study — move the first stop
work_blocks.prompt: Make two 8–10 cm thumbnails with the same three simple forms. In A, cluster the forms evenly. In B, move one form away from the others. Keep size and value as similar as you can.
work_blocks.bounded_choice: Choose which form to isolate and where to place it.
work_blocks.observable_criterion: Your notes identify which form arrives first in each thumbnail and cite spacing or placement as evidence.
work_blocks.attempt_before_support: Complete both thumbnails and record a first impression before opening the placement cue.
work_blocks.optional_cue: If the isolated form still does not lead, enlarge the open space around it without darkening or enlarging the form.
work_blocks.support_fade: Close the model and cue before beginning the independent composition.

work_blocks.title: Independent studio — design a visual path
work_blocks.prompt: Choose a subject or use abstract forms. Plan three possible thumbnails, select one, and develop a composition with an intended first, second, and third stop.
objective_constraints: Use three or more forms or areas.
Name one intended focal point before developing the study.
Use at least two hierarchy variables.
Run one visual-path check and make or deliberately decline one revision with a reason.
learner_owned_choices: whether critique evidence calls for revision
work_blocks.permitted_support: Definitions, the technique sequence, a parallel example, material alternatives, and criterion restatement remain available. No one else may choose the focal point or alter the scored composition.

work_blocks.title: Reflection — trace your decisions
prompts: Name your intended first, second, and third stops. Cite one visible feature at each location.
Compare your preserved intermediate state with the later state. What variable changed, and what did that change do?
Which tradeoff did you accept: a steeper route with quieter later areas, or a subtler route with more openness? Explain from the work.

work_blocks.title: Private critique — evidence before advice
protocol: Describe the first area noticed without judging it.
Point to the contrast, spacing, scale, edge, repetition, or direction that produced that stop.
Compare the observed path with the artist’s stated intent.
Ask one genuine question about the route.
Offer two revision possibilities; the artist may choose either, invent another, or keep the work with evidence.
work_blocks.private_route: Use the protocol on your own work after turning it away for one minute. No peer, audience, or public post is required.

work_blocks.title: Knowledge check — explain the mechanism
prompts: A large pale form and a small dark isolated form share a page. Give two reasons the small form might arrive first.
Why can increasing contrast everywhere weaken an intended hierarchy?
Name one situation in which a subtle hierarchy could serve an artist’s intent better than a steep one.
work_blocks.note: This check supports concept understanding but does not replace the independent visual work.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several major areas use similarly strong value jumps, hard edges, or detail, so the intended focal point is not a reliably distinct first stop.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner states and supports an intent for distributed, ambiguous, or nonhierarchical attention.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The learner names a focal point, but two separate three-second checks identify another area first and the learner cannot cite a hierarchy variable supporting the intended area.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner revises the stated intent to match a defensible observed route.

remediation_paths.different_instruction: Reduce the work to a three-value map. Label each major area light, middle, or dark; circle every large jump. Keep one large jump and lower the others in a fresh thumbnail.
remediation_paths.supported_attempt: Use three forms and only pencil pressure. Create one dark-light jump at the intended first stop; keep the other forms middle or pale.
remediation_paths.self_noticing_cue: Squint or use the tactile value labels: can you locate one strongest difference?
remediation_paths.fresh_retry: Make a new thumbnail with different placements and run a new three-second check.

remediation_paths.different_instruction: Cover the work except for the intended focal point and one competing area. Compare only those two; choose whether value, scale, isolation, edge, or direction should separate them.
remediation_paths.supported_attempt: On scrap paper, redraw the two areas and change exactly one chosen variable.
remediation_paths.self_noticing_cue: Name the changed variable before deciding which area arrives first.
remediation_paths.fresh_retry: Return all areas in a fresh thumbnail and test the intended path without the model in view.

legitimate_variation: Difference from the Academy model is never an error and resemblance earns no extra credit.
Subject, abstraction, medium, format, style, palette, and mood remain learner-owned choices.
A focal point may be created through value, scale, placement, isolation, repetition, edge, direction, or another defensible visual relationship.
A learner may support a steep, subtle, distributed, ambiguous, or deliberately nonhierarchical route when the evidence matches the stated intent.
A learner may revise the artwork, revise the stated intention, or keep the result with an evidence-based reason.
